rust_summary: `native_upgrade_block_entity(data_version, tag)` and `native_upgrade_entity(data_version, tag)`: block entity and entity NBT saved at an older DataVersion, upgraded as the chunk loader upgrades them.
doc_summary: `native_upgrade_block_entity(data_version, tag)` and `native_upgrade_entity(data_version, tag)` give a block entity's or an entity's NBT (a compound) as the chunk loader upgrades it when it was saved at `data_version`: the same fixes, from that DataVersion up to the current one, so a block entity or entity of an older world, or a blueprint that carries its DataVersion, comes out in the current format. A block entity whose `id` the version doesn't know, and data at the current DataVersion or newer, come back as they are. Fixes of the whole chunk (the blocks around a block entity, the removal of bed block entities) don't run on one block entity. Bundles need "hooks": @API:upgrade_entities@.
